findings.issue: The -8.8% FCF yield appears on the grounding surface only under the Trailing-twelve-months block (Facts: 'FCF yield -8.8%'; highlight key fcfYield = FCF Yield (TTM) = -8.8%). No FY25 FCF yield is given. Labeling it 'FY25 FCF yield' attaches a TTM figure to the wrong period, and it does not tie to the FY25 FCF of -$97.8M against the $596.5M market cap (which would imply roughly -16%). The same TTM figure is again presented as FY25 in risks.idiosyncratic[0]: 'FY25 free cash flow was -$97.8M and the FCF yield -8.8%.'
findings.fix: Relabel -8.8% as the trailing-twelve-month FCF yield (or drop it), keeping the -$97.8M explicitly as the FY25 free cash flow. Apply the same relabel in risks.idiosyncratic[0].
findings.note: Fixed in both places. cashflowCommentary now reads 'The trailing-twelve-month FCF yield was -8.8%'; risks.idiosyncratic[0] now reads 'the trailing-twelve-month FCF yield -8.8%'. FY25 FCF kept explicit at -$97.8M; no invented FY25 FCF-yield figure. The -8.8% now matches its TTM source period.

findings.quote: The reward-to-risk is roughly balanced, which supports a HOLD rather than a directional call.
findings.issue: With probability-weighted value of ~$3.61 vs the $3.59 price (expected upside ~+0.4%) and a Bear at $2.10 (-41.5%), the reward/risk is heavily downside-skewed (R ~0.01x), not 'roughly balanced.' The thesis makes the same claim ('so risk and reward are balanced'), while finalRecommendation.body[1] states the opposite: 'the reward does not compensate for the downside.' The HOLD is sound (weighted value ~= price), but 'balanced reward/risk' overstates symmetry and conflicts with the final section.
findings.fix: Reword to say the shares screen fairly valued (expected value ~= current price) so there is no directional edge, and align the phrasing with finalRecommendation's point that the ~flat upside does not compensate for the -41.5% bear downside.
findings.note: Reworded in both places. scenarioCommentary now reads 'The thin upside does not offset the far larger bear-case downside, so the shares look fairly valued with no directional edge'; thesis.body now reads 'the bear case dwarfs the thin upside, so I see no directional edge.' The false-symmetry claim is gone and both align with finalRecommendation. (body[1]'s 'The setup is balanced rather than directional' is immediately qualified by 'the reward does not compensate for the downside', so it does not re-assert symmetry.)

findings.quote: the six-month operating loss narrowed to $(17,285) thousand from $(52,113) thousand as SG&A fell 20.8% and R&D dropped to $19,607 thousand
findings.issue: These exact figures — the $(17,285)/$(52,113) six-month operating loss, the 20.8% SG&A decline and the $19,607 thousand R&D — are introduced and argued in financials.incomeCommentary and already pointed to in executiveSummary.catalysts[0] and analystCommentary. Re-quoting them verbatim in the final section repeats rather than refers back in words, against the house style 'introduce each figure once per section and refer back in words afterwards.'
findings.fix: In finalRecommendation, refer back to the narrowing operating loss and cost cuts in words (e.g., 'the sharply narrower six-month operating loss on lower SG&A and R&D') without re-quoting the thousands-level figures already given in the financials section.
findings.note: Fixed. finalRecommendation.body[0] now refers back in words — 'the six-month operating loss has narrowed sharply as the 2025 Restructuring Plan lowered SG&A and R&D' — with none of the thousands-level figures re-quoted.
